name: Personalised Wealth Advice
title: Personalised Wealth Advice
answer: Personalised wealth advice covers the generation of investment recommendations tailored to an individual's goals, time horizon, risk tolerance, tax situation, and constraints. It sits within portfolio construction and spans asset allocation, security selection, rebalancing, and tax management. The advice can be delivered through digital platforms, human advisors using software, or hybrid models. It differs from generic model portfolios because the output depends on client-specific data and preferences. The atlas tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which can form part of the investable universe for such advice.

sections.body: Personalised wealth advice covers the generation of investment recommendations tailored to an individual's goals, time horizon, risk tolerance, tax situation, and constraints. It sits within portfolio construction and spans asset allocation, security selection, rebalancing, and tax management. The advice can be delivered through digital platforms, human advisors using software, or hybrid models. It differs from generic model portfolios because the output depends on client-specific data and preferences. The atlas tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which can form part of the investable universe for such advice.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The infrastructure for personalised wealth advice typically includes market data feeds, client account systems, portfolio accounting, and risk engines. It runs on cloud compute and APIs that connect custodian data, trading systems, and reporting layers. Many implementations use large language models for client communication and document parsing, alongside traditional optimization libraries. Data quality and latency matter because advice may need to reflect current prices and positions. The atlas lists 732 AI tools, a broad set that includes analytics and client engagement software.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done through a combination of risk profiling, optimization, and simulation. Advisors and platforms often use mean-variance optimization, factor models, or goals-based investing to translate client inputs into portfolio weights. AI methods such as clustering, forecasting, and natural language processing can enrich the process, for example by extracting goals from client conversations. Rebalancing and tax-loss harvesting are typically rule-based or optimized over time. The atlas lists 732 AI tools, which reflects the wide range of software available for these tasks.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Governance covers fiduciary duty, suitability, disclosure, data privacy, and model risk management. Firms must keep audit trails of advice, explain recommendations, and manage conflicts of interest. Client data provenance, consent, and security are central, especially when third-party models or cloud services are used. The atlas tracks 146 active AI lawsuits and 215 compliance and regulation pages, which shows the level of legal and regulatory activity surrounding AI in finance. Model explainability and bias testing are increasingly expected by regulators and clients.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more continuous, data-driven personalization and greater use of generative AI for client interaction. We can expect tighter integration of tax, estate, and cash flow planning into portfolio advice. Regulatory frameworks for AI in finance are still developing, and their shape will affect what firms can deploy. The atlas tracks 354 merger and acquisition filings, which suggests ongoing consolidation and investment in the tooling that supports this work. Human oversight is likely to remain a feature of advice for the foreseeable future.
